tagline: Use Linear's Figma integration for design previews, and GAIA for the issue, GitHub and Slack work around handoff
metaTitle: Linear Figma Integration: Attach Designs to Issues
metaDescription: Linear's Figma integration previews designs in issues, and its Figma plugin files issues from a frame. GAIA handles the Linear, GitHub and Slack side.
intro:
To integrate Figma with Linear, turn on the built-in integration from the integrations settings. After that, a design file or frame link pasted into an issue or comment shows a live preview of the design. In the design app, the official plugin lets you create an issue from a selected frame, or link an existing one, without leaving the file. Those two pieces together are the official integration: designs attached to issues, and issues created from designs.

If your team also runs GitHub and Slack, connect them natively as well. The GitHub integration links pull requests to issues and moves issues forward as pull requests open and merge. The Slack integration creates issues from messages and posts issue updates to channels. With all three on, all four tools share links and previews without another tool in the middle.

GAIA does not connect to Figma, so it cannot read frames, versions, or comments in your files. What it handles is the work around design handoff in Linear, GitHub and Slack: it creates issues that carry the links you give it, reacts when issues are created, updated, or commented on, and messages designers and engineers in Slack when something needs them. Event triggers are available in GAIA, so these workflows can run as soon as an issue changes, not only on a schedule.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues with the design link attached
useCases.description: Paste a Figma link in chat and describe the work. GAIA creates the Linear issue in the right team with a title, a description, and the link, so the integration shows the preview.

useCases.title: Turn design review notes into issues
useCases.description: Paste your review notes or a list of requested changes, and GAIA files one issue per item with the related design link, plus the assignee, labels, and cycle you name.

useCases.title: Tell designers when implementation starts
useCases.description: A workflow triggered by issue updates checks for design-labeled issues that moved to In Progress and messages the designer in Slack with the issue link.

useCases.title: Route engineering questions on design issues to Slack
useCases.description: When someone comments on a design-labeled issue, GAIA posts the comment and the issue link to your design channel in Slack, so designers see questions without watching the issue tracker.

useCases.title: Send a weekly design handoff report
useCases.description: Every week, GAIA searches for design-related issues and sends you a summary: what is waiting on design, what is in development, and which issues have no design link in their description.

howItWorks.step: Turn on the Figma integration, then connect Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Enable the integration for design previews, and install the plugin if designers want to file issues from Figma. Then connect Linear to GAIA from the integrations page, plus Slack or GitHub if your workflows use them.

howItWorks.step: Describe the workflow in plain English
howItWorks.description: Create a workflow, for example: "When an issue with the label design moves to In Progress, message its designer in #design on Slack." Or ask in chat to file issues from a design link.

howItWorks.step: GAIA runs it in the background
howItWorks.description: Triggered workflows run when the event arrives, scheduled ones on your timetable, and each reports what it did. Destructive actions such as deleting issues or comments follow your approval settings.

faqs.question: How does GAIA match design frames to issues automatically?
faqs.answer: It does not. GAIA has no connection to design files, so it cannot search them or match frames by name. The link comes from you or your team: paste the design URL into the issue (GAIA adds it when it creates the issue for you) or create the issue from the design file with the official plugin.

faqs.question: Can GAIA embed design previews directly in issues?
faqs.answer: The preview comes from the official design integration, not from GAIA. Once it is on, any design link in an issue description or comment renders as a preview, including links GAIA adds when it creates or updates issues.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with branches for design versioning?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA cannot see design branches, versions, or merges. If you want the issue to reflect that a design is final, have the designer change the issue state or add a label, and a GAIA workflow can react to that change.

faqs.question: How do I integrate Figma with Linear?
faqs.answer: Turn on the integration from the integrations settings and sign in with your design account. Paste design links into issues to get previews. Designers can also install the official plugin to create or link issues from a frame.

faqs.question: How do I connect GitHub, Slack and the design app to my issues?
faqs.answer: Use the native integration for each: the design integration for previews, GitHub for linking pull requests and updating issue status, and Slack for creating issues from messages and posting updates. Add GAIA when you want routines across them, such as messaging a designer in Slack when an issue starts development, or a weekly handoff summary.

faqs.question: Is there an official integration for design previews?
faqs.answer: Yes. The issue tracker ships its own integration and plugin for design files. GAIA does not replace either one; it works on the issue, GitHub and Slack side of the handoff.
